explanation: Compile-time polymorphism, unlike runtime polymorphism achieved through virtual functions, leverages templates and `constexpr` functions to perform computations and generate specialized code during compilation.  This avoids runtime overhead associated with virtual function calls and branching. The compiler generates distinct code paths for each type used with the template, effectively creating multiple versions of the function at compile time.  Memory layout is affected as each specialized instantiation might have a different size and structure depending on the underlying types. Performance gains are significant when dealing with large datasets or performance-critical sections because there's no runtime dispatch.
